title: Memory key body
description: An identity publishes the PUBLIC half of its X25519 memory key (register rows D12 and DK272; spec-delta S1604; docs/private-memory-run-design.md 1), so a principal-agent pair can seal a private memory scope to each other's keys from a second machine. `did` is the issuer (an agent signs its own; a sponsor does not publish for it), `name` the entry (memory-1, memory-2), `public_key` the RAW 32-byte key in base64url without padding (43 characters), `at` the time, `revokes` the record id of the entry a rotation replaces. The log refuses a signer who is not the identity (memory_key_wrong_issuer), an identity with no passport (memory_key_unknown_identity), anything that is not exactly 32 raw bytes, such as a PKCS8 or SPKI blob that could carry private material (memory_key_private_material), a second live key (memory_key_live: name the one it replaces in `revokes`) and a `revokes` that is not this identity's live entry (memory_key_revokes_unknown). The latest un-revoked entry is the live key (`memoryKey(did)`). Chain: none (prev is null).
